Getting started
Setup & reference
Tap the pencil to write; tap the keyboard for shortcut keys.
Tap a saved Snippet to use it.
In Herdr, tap Switch to choose a Space or task.
Reorder Snippets
Tap ✎, then long-press a Snippet and drag it into place.
Edit a Snippet
Tap ✎, then tap a saved Snippet to edit it.
Recent projects
In Herdr, long press New Workspace to choose a recent project.
Close a Tab
In Herdr, double-tap a numbered Tab to close it.
Close a Space
In Switch, double-tap a Space to close it.
Tab actions
In Herdr, long press a Tab to open its menu.
Photos & files
Tap the image key for photos; long press it for files.
Restore your draft

Photos & file attachments
Tap for photos, long press for any file
Tap the image key beside Home to open the system photo picker with recent photos and videos.
Long-press the same image key to choose any files, including PDFs, archives and other image formats.
To attach an image, video or file copied from another app, use Paste in the shortcut keys. Image and file paste from your phone keyboard also works when the keyboard offers it.

In SSH or Mosh, files are copied to the connected computer. In Local Arch, they are copied into your phone’s Arch environment. Wait for copying to finish; the file paths then appear in the terminal input.

Files keep their original contents. The app adds no fixed file-size, format or attachment-count limit. The system picker can limit how many items you select, and your chat tool decides which files it can read.
Typing & recovering a draft
Send, Enter, Undo and switching tabs
Tap Type or the pencil button to edit a draft. Tap the keyboard button to return to shortcut keys. Swipe left across the helper area to reach Snippets.
Your phone keyboard’s Send action pastes the draft without adding Enter. This lets you review it in the remote program before submitting.
Tap ↵ beside the draft to paste it and press Enter. With an empty draft, ↵ sends Enter on its own.
After sending, tap the curved-arrow Undo button to restore the last draft for editing or resending. Commands that have already run remain in effect.
Your draft stays available when you switch connection tabs or reopen the app. Check the active tab before sending: the draft goes to the selected terminal.
Tap the microphone beside the draft to dictate. Allow microphone access when asked, tap Stop to finish, then review the text before sending.
When Snippets are pinned above the keyboard, use the small chevron beside the draft or shortcut keys to hide or show them. Change this placement in Settings → Snippets.
Shortcut keys & modifiers
Ctrl, Alt, Shift, repeat and custom layouts
Tap Ctrl, Alt or Shift, then another key to send that combination. By default, the modifier turns off after one accepted key.
For repeated combinations, choose One-shot + double-tap lock in Settings → Keyboard. Double-tap a modifier to keep it on; tap it again to unlock.
Long press a navigation key to repeat it. Turn Long-press repeat on or off in Settings → Keyboard.
Use Settings → Keyboard → Edit accessory keys to add or remove keys and drag them into order. Save the layout when you finish. A custom layout with extra keys can have more pages; swipe through them.
Terminal text & touch
Select output, open links, show the keyboard and zoom
Long-press ordinary terminal output to start selecting text. Drag the selection handles, then choose Copy or Select all. The keyboard hides to leave room for selection.
Long-press a link to see its actions, including Copy link and Open link when available.
In a mouse-enabled terminal interface, double-tap ordinary output to show the keyboard. A single tap can be sent to the remote program as a mouse click.
Enable Pinch to zoom in Settings → Appearance, then use two fingers to adjust the current terminal’s text size.
Connection tabs & tmux
Duplicate tabs, find text, export output and switch sessions
Double-tap a connection tab to open another connection with the same settings. The app asks for credentials again when they were not retained.
Long-press a connection tab for its actions. Use Find to search retained terminal output, Export transcript to save it, or Disconnect and Close to manage the connection.
The stacked-window button in the top bar lists app connection tabs. The stacked-window key beside the keyboard opens the connected computer’s tmux session selector.
Enable Show tmux session selector in Settings → Sessions & Background to choose Start new session, Attach or Open shell after connecting.
Choose Focus fullscreen from a connection tab’s actions to give the terminal more space. Use Back to leave focus mode.
Files on a connected computer
Open, select, move and transfer files or folders
Open Files from a connection tab’s actions. Tap a folder to enter it. Tap a file to download and open it with a phone app; older Android versions ask you to choose a destination first.
Long-press a file or folder to select it and reveal actions such as Copy, Cut, Rename and Delete. Swipe the action row horizontally if an action is off screen.
To copy or move an item on the connected computer, select it, choose Copy or Cut, enter the destination folder, then tap Paste.
Tap From phone, then Choose files or Choose folder to upload into the folder currently open on the connected computer.
Select an item and choose Download to use Downloads on supported Android versions, or Save to… to choose a phone folder. Folder downloads include their contents.
Pull down on the file list to refresh it after changes made elsewhere. Use Up to return to the parent folder.

Herdr setup for phones & foldables
Recommended settings, status dots and how to apply changes

Configure Herdr on the computer running your SSH or Mosh session. The Android app does not install or configure Herdr for you. On Linux/macOS the usual file is ~/.config/herdr/config.toml; run herdr --help on that computer to check the actual path, including any HERDR_CONFIG_PATH or XDG_CONFIG_HOME override.

Back up the existing file. Merge these supported keys into its existing [ui] table, keeping your other settings and keybindings. Add [ui] only if it is missing; do not create a second [ui] table or replace the whole file with this example.

[ui]
mouse_capture = true
mobile_width_threshold = 64
status_indicators = "dots"

mouse_capture lets Herdr respond to touch-derived clicks and menus. A mobile_width_threshold of 64 keeps Switch on narrow terminals; wider terminals, including an unfolded screen with enough columns, show the sidebar beside the terminal. The threshold counts terminal columns, not pixels: larger text leaves fewer columns. Avoid 160 if you want the unfolded sidebar.

Optional space-saving settings in the same [ui] table: pane_gaps = false, pane_outer_borders = false and pane_scrollbars = false. If you want new tabs to open without a naming prompt, also set prompt_new_tab_name = false. These are preferences; keep the decorations or prompt you find useful.

For the compact Space → task list in the expanded sidebar, add the following key to that same [ui] table only if your Herdr build supports it. grouped_sidebar, grouped mobile task lists, numbered top tabs and compact task labels are features of our development Herdr build. The Android APK does not supply these patches, and adding a key cannot add them to an unsupported Herdr executable.
grouped_sidebar = true

status_indicators = \"dots\" keeps the colored task status dots. In the development grouped list, green means idle and yellow means working. The status dot sits at the left, followed by the number and task name; the extra separator after the number is removed. A gray dot means the status is unknown.

Git arrows and worktree markers need Git metadata from Herdr or an existing status provider. Missing markers do not mean a clean repository. A checkmark means an explicitly reported clean worktree; it does not mean every commit has been pushed. Automatic task names from Codex terminal titles also require the compatible development Herdr server.

Run herdr config check, then use the Herdr menu → reload config in the intended session and read any diagnostics. If an option is unsupported, leave it out. Check that task selection and menus work, and that folding or unfolding chooses the layout you want. To undo the settings, restore your backup and reload.

After installing a new Herdr executable, use Herdr menu → detach, then attach to the same session again. Reconnecting a Mosh transport can keep the old client running. Your server, Spaces and tasks can stay running; do not stop the server to apply a layout change.
Prefer help with the setup? Copy the instructions below and send them to an agent with access to the connected computer. They ask for configuration changes while preserving your running tasks.

Configure Herdr for Terminal Spike on the computer my SSH/Mosh connection uses. Identify the host, actual executable/version and config path, respecting HERDR_CONFIG_PATH and XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Back up the config and merge supported [ui] keys: mouse_capture=true, mobile_width_threshold=64 and status_indicators=\"dots\". For compact panes, suggest pane_gaps=false, pane_outer_borders=false and pane_scrollbars=false. Enable grouped_sidebar=true only if this Herdr build supports it. Explain that grouped task lists, numbered top tabs, compact labels and automatic task names require a compatible development Herdr build; an Android APK or width setting alone cannot supply them. Keep existing Git-status providers and report missing metadata without inventing a clean state. Preserve other settings, keybindings, connections and running tasks; do not duplicate TOML tables. Do not replace binaries, patch source, stop servers, kill panes or recreate workspaces. Validate with herdr config check, reload the intended session, inspect diagnostics, and explain any needed detach/reattach. Report the minimal diff, rollback steps and checks actually performed, without secrets.

Tailscale setup
Set up your phone and computer once
Computer — Install Tailscale on your laptop or desktop. Sign in and keep it connected and awake.
Phone — Install the Tailscale app and connect to the same tailnet. Terminal Spike uses this connection automatically.
For a terminal, enable SSH on your computer. In Terminal Spike, use its Tailscale name or 100.x address, your computer username, and SSH key or password. The usual SSH port is 22.
Get Tailscale
Code server setup
Run code-server on your computer, then open its address here
1. Computer — Install code-server on the computer with your projects. The official installation guide is linked below.

2. Run code-server. Check http://127.0.0.1:8080 in that computer’s browser. Find the password in ~/.config/code-server/config.yaml. Keep password authentication enabled and bind-addr set to 127.0.0.1:8080.
3. With Tailscale connected, run this in another terminal. Approve HTTPS if prompted. Use an unused HTTPS port if 9443 is taken:
tailscale serve --bg --https=9443 http://127.0.0.1:8080
4. Phone — Connect Tailscale. Tap Code server and paste the printed .ts.net HTTPS address, including :9443. Enter the code-server password. Remember on this device saves it encrypted after login.
Switch tabs to return to your terminal. Use ⋮ for the server address, password and layout. Browser is a separate tab with its own address bar.
Cannot connect? Keep the computer awake and check that Tailscale and code-server are running. Use the printed HTTPS hostname; localhost on the phone refers to the phone itself.

Make Herdr your own

Using Herdr? If your panel looks different from our promotional screenshots, ask your agent to adjust your Herdr settings and layout. For example: “Move the Switch button to the bottom-left corner.” You can customize the rest of the panel too. Your phone displays the Herdr layout you configure.
